findings.summary: SIRIUS_QUERY_WATCHDOG_SECS parsing accepts values the error message claims it rejects. std::strtoull(env, &end, 10) consumes a leading '-' and wraps, and ERANGE is never checked, so `end == env || *end != '\0'` passes and the "must be a non-negative integer" throw never fires for a negative value.
findings.failure_scenario: export SIRIUS_QUERY_WATCHDOG_SECS=-1 (a common "disable" idiom, and the string the doc implies is rejected): parsed = 18446744073709551615, watchdog_secs likewise; at line 165 std::chrono::seconds(watchdog_secs) narrows to seconds(-1), so `now - last_progress >= seconds(-1)` is true on the very first 250 ms poll and fail_stalled_query() kills EVERY query with "no scheduling progress for 18446744073709551615s". Values >= ~9.2e9 (seconds->nanoseconds common-type overflow) misbehave the same way.
findings.fix: Reject a leading '-' (and whitespace) before strtoull, check errno == ERANGE, and clamp the accepted range to something representable, e.g. `if (parsed > 86400) throw invalid_input_exception(...)`; keep the message aligned with what is actually enforced.
